epic.title: epic-418-followon — make agents use the MCP door instead of the CLI
epic.intent_and_why: Agents drive their spines through the MCP door and never touch the engine CLI directly; the CLI is an implementation detail behind the door. Entry definitions stay configurable so the work is OS-agnostic by construction. Anything an operator must remember to do by hand is a defect in the tool.

definition_of_done: A dispatched crew drives its own spine through the door, measured from its own call record.
A respawned agent on the same assignment resumes its lease rather than force-claiming it.
Constellation agent instructions name the door and not the engine CLI.
No shipped entry definition hardcodes an interpreter or an absolute path.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: Every claim about what happened brings its evidence; a control must reproduce the defect before a fix is believed.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Measured from the driving agent's own call record, never from the engine's refusals counter.
good_enough.appetite: One bounded wave; keep out the easy failures rather than making it foolproof.

hard_constraints: docs/agents/* edits are a human's call
No merge or push to main while the human is AFK
Planning makes no direct gh or network mutation
fixed_decisions: The lease keys on the assignment, not the process instance
Identity is derived from the spine's own work_id, never hand-typed
The CLI door stays as a fallback; F is additive
Agents do not know about the engine CLI; the CLI is used only behind the MCP door
Mechanical setup is the tool's job, not the operator's

current_wave.objective: Hand every dispatched crew its own spine and a derived, assignment-keyed identity, so an agent drives its own task's spine through the door and a respawn resumes rather than force-claims.
exit_criteria: A crew dispatched through run_crew.py receives SPINE_FILE bound to its own spine and SPINE_SESSION carrying an assignment-keyed identity, verified from the child's environment rather than from prose.
The lease identity is derived from the spine's own work_id plus the claiming role, excludes the attempt tail, and is not hand-typed anywhere in the shipped path.
A second dispatch on the same assignment resumes the lease idempotently, with no force and no takeover recorded — proven by a control that reproduces the force-claim before the change.
A cold reviewer independent of the implementer has approved the change.

#555 is carried unchanged and unworked. It stays in this wave because it is a launched identity that may not be silently dropped; its terms are preserved verbatim and no spend is authorized against it this wave. Its disposition returns to the human.

issues.title: run_crew.py binds each crew's door to its own spine and derives an assignment-keyed lease identity
issues.desired_outcome: crew_env() hands the child SPINE_FILE for that crew's own spine and SPINE_SESSION as constellation/<work-id>/<gate>/<role>, derived from the spine's work_id and the role, with no attempt tail. A respawn on the same assignment resumes its lease instead of force-claiming it.
issues.useful_now: It is the single wire between two constructs that already exist, and it is what makes a dispatched agent able to use the door at all.
issues.appetite: One bounded change to the crew launcher plus tests. Not a rewrite of the engine or the door.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: A control that reproduces today's behaviour first — a crew whose door binds to the demo spine, and a relaunch that must force-claim — then the same two cases passing after the change. Measured from the child's actual environment and the spine's lease record, never from prose.
issues.implementation_latitude: Choose how the spine path and role reach crew_env(). Preserve the existing lease semantics exactly; the engine's claim() is not to be modified. Do not open per-call spine addressing in the door.
hard_constraints_no_gos: Do not weaken _identity_violation or the from_child path confinement
Do not touch settings.json or docs/agents/*
No merge or push to main; local commits only
local_unknowns: Whether the role is already available at the crew_env() call site or must be threaded in
Whether any existing caller depends on crew_env() not setting SPINE_*

completed_outcomes.outcome: run_crew.py binds each dispatched crew's door to its own spine and derives an assignment-keyed lease identity; merged to main as 27a5adf5.
completed_outcomes.evidence: Three cold review rounds found three real defects, all fixed. Suite 2494 passed / 1 skipped / 1089 subtests on merged main. Two of four crews drove their spines through the door (24 and 22 door calls), leases assignment-keyed with no attempt tail, claimed and released.

wave_evidence.claim: Binding the door to a crew's own spine makes agents use it
wave_evidence.expected: A correctly bound crew uses the door instead of the CLI
wave_evidence.observed: PARTLY FALSIFIED. Four crews ran with a correctly bound door. The two told explicitly in their handoff to prefer the door made 24 and 22 calls; the reviewer made 0 and drove its survey through the CLI; one rework crew made 0 and never touched its spine at all. Binding is necessary and not sufficient.
wave_evidence.source: mcp_calls.jsonl per gate, and the four spine files' lease and gate状態

wave_evidence.claim: The lease identity fix takes effect regardless of how the agent reaches the engine
wave_evidence.expected: A crew claims with the assignment identity
wave_evidence.observed: FALSIFIED for the CLI route. The reviewer's lease was constellation/.../g2-review/reviewer/attempt-1 — the attempt-tagged name it read out of its own prompt, which build_crew_argv fills with session_name(). The derived identity only takes effect through the door.
wave_evidence.source: REVIEW_SURVEY.json engine_session, and build_crew_argv at scripts/run_crew.py:302

wave_evidence.claim: run_crew.py's cli backend is usable as shipped
wave_evidence.expected: A spawned crew can do a crew's work
wave_evidence.observed: FALSIFIED. build_crew_argv passes no --allowedTools and no --permission-mode. Every dispatch today needed a hand-written gitignored .claude/settings.local.json in the worktree first. All 7 prior crews in this epic used the external backend instead.
FALSIFIED. .mcp.json hardcodes "command": "python3", which on this host is the interpreter WITHOUT pytest and on the owner's Windows box is not a command at all.

wave_evidence.expected: Its Python guidance matches the machine
wave_evidence.observed: FALSIFIED. It names py as the broken interpreter; py and python are the same install carrying pytest 9.1.1 and /usr/bin/python3 is the one without it. Three handoffs today carried an inline correction to work around it.
